title: From coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to continuum models of biomolecular condensation
abstract: Biomolecular condensation contributes to cellular organization and the regulation of numerous biochemical processes. Capturing its dynamics on large spatio-temporal scales requires a macroscopic model that accurately describes both thermodynamic forces and molecular transport. Here, we investigate the applicability of the Cahn-Hilliard equation for modeling phase-separation dynamics in intrinsically disordered proteins. Using the low-complexity domain of FUS as a model system for biomolecular condensation, we perform coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to infer the free-energy functional and mobility coefficient entering the Cahn-Hilliard equation. The resulting continuum model accurately describes the growth of initial concentration fluctuations in the spinodal regime and the subsequent morphological evolution of the concentration fields during coarsening. We find that the free-energy functional is transferable across different stages of phase separation, whereas the mobility is not. During coarsening, we identify two kinetic regimes characterized by distinct mobilities, which persist even when a concentration-dependent mobility is introduced.
relevance_reason: Uses coarse-grained molecular dynamics of an intrinsically disordered protein to infer free-energy and mobility parameters for a continuum model, satisfying (a), (b), and (c).

title: Stepwise unknotting of complex polymer knots under nanochannel confinement
abstract: We performed Langevin dynamics simulations to investigate the unknotting dynamics of knotted DNA molecules confined within nanochannels, specifically examining three different torus knot types: 31, 51, and 71 knots, and the 61 twist knot. 51 and 71 knots typically undergo stepwise unknotting, in which knots are partially untied into a simpler knot topology when they first reach the chain end, subsequently requiring multiple rounds of topological simplification before being fully untied. In contrast, as would be expected, simple trefoil knots untie directly as they approach the chain ends, following a one-step process. We further examined the impact of nanochannel size on unknotting dynamics and topological changes across different knot types. For the complex 51 and 71 knots, stepwise unknotting is the prevalent mechanism, and increasing the spatial confinement prolongs the entire stepwise unknotting process. For the 61 knot, the primary mechanism of untying is also sequential, with ∼20% of the knots untying in a single step. In addition, the topological changes induced by both confinement and knot types are found to be correlated with the extended unknotting times; while the topology of the knot (twist vs torus) dictates the possible unknotting pathways, the rate of unknotting is modulated by the channel size.
relevance_reason: Langevin dynamics simulations of coarse-grained knotted DNA in nanochannels satisfy (a) via explicit bead-chain representation, (b) via MD-type dynamics, and (c) via application to polymer topology.

title: Nudged elastic membranes for constructing reduced two-dimensional potential energy surfaces
abstract: Minimum-energy paths and intrinsic reaction coordinates are central tools for analyzing chemical reactions. As one-dimensional objects, however, individual paths do not provide a continuous representation of the surrounding potential energy surface (PES), including the arrangement of adjacent valleys, ridges, and higher-order saddle regions. We introduce the nudged elastic membrane method, which constructs a two-dimensional reduced PES in a selected region of configuration space using energies and forces, without requiring Hessian evaluations. The method is demonstrated for a three-dimensional analytical model and for triplet formaldehyde. In both cases, the membrane recovers known reaction-path and stationary-point regions. For formaldehyde, it also reveals a previously unreported second-order saddle point on the fitted PES. Structures extracted from the membrane provide starting points for subsequent stationary-point refinement.
relevance_reason: Nudged elastic membrane method constructs a reduced PES from energies and forces and is applied to formaldehyde, satisfying (a) explicit atomic PES, (b) NEB-like path/PES methodology, and (c) method advance.

title: Exact decomposition and approximate power-law scaling of truncation errors in multiconfigurational wave functions
abstract: Although truncation errors in multiconfigurational expansions are known empirically to correlate with the discarded weight, a rigorous, scheme-independent theoretical foundation for this relation is lacking. From an orthogonal decomposition of the full configuration interaction (FCI) wave function, we derive an exact expression ΔE = ω(Ed − EFCI)/(1 − ω) and validate it across 20 systems, four orbital representations, and four truncation schemes. In the weak-truncation regime (ω ≪ 1), the mean discarded excitation energy varies slowly, yielding an approximate power law ΔE ∝ ωα, where α depends systematically on the truncation strategy (0.86–0.91) and electronic structure, yet the error remains dominated by ω. Because ω requires the exact FCI wave function, it serves as an a posteriori diagnostic. This framework provides a unified theoretical basis for comparing truncation and orbital schemes and rationalizes the empirical success of coefficient-based selection methods.
relevance_reason: Post-Hartree-Fock multiconfigurational wavefunction truncation-error theory satisfies (a) explicit electronic-structure systems, (b) post-HF method development, and (c) advances quantum-chemistry methodology.
